pharm: Aqueous extract of common wheat (Triticum vulgare); promotes fibroblast/granulation tissue activity
quick: Apply to affected area 1-2 times daily (formulation-dependent)

summary: Triticum vulgare extract is an aqueous extract of common wheat used topically to promote tissue repair and wound healing. It is applied to skin lesions, ulcers, burns, abrasions, and other wounds to stimulate granulation tissue formation and re-epithelialization. It is available in creams, foams, gauze dressings, sprays, and suppositories/region-specific forms. It is not FDA-approved; this record is based on European/SmPC and manufacturer labeling. It is generally well tolerated topically, with allergic reactions being the main concern, especially in those sensitized to wheat.
indications: Topical treatment to promote healing of skin lesions, wounds, ulcers, and abrasions
Adjunct in management of burns and dermal ulcers (e.g., pressure or venous ulcers)
Local anti-inflammatory/repair support in certain anogenital or dermatologic conditions (formulation-specific)

dosage.d: Apply to the affected area as directed on the product
dosage.n: Useful for larger or weeping areas

admin: Clean the affected area before application
Apply the appropriate formulation (cream, foam, gauze, spray) as directed to the lesion

moa: Triticum vulgare (common wheat) extract is proposed to stimulate the proliferation and activity of fibroblasts and to promote chemotaxis and angiogenesis, accelerating formation of granulation tissue and re-epithelialization. This supports faster repair of damaged skin and mucosa. The active constituents are not fully characterized.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to Triticum vulgare (wheat) extract or formulation components
relative: Application to grossly infected wounds without appropriate treatment
monitor: Wound healing progress and signs of infection

preg: Topical use is generally considered acceptable with minimal systemic absorption. Use during pregnancy as directed by a clinician; avoid extensive application unless necessary.
lact: Topical use is generally acceptable, but avoid applying to the breast or nipple area to prevent infant exposure.
renal: Not applicable for topical use; negligible systemic absorption.
hepatic: Not applicable for topical use; negligible systemic absorption.

minor: Other topical agents applied to the same site - apply separately to avoid dilution/interference

common: Mild local burning or stinging on application
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with swelling or breathing difficulty

monitoring: Wound healing response and reduction in lesion size
Local skin tolerance and signs of allergy
Signs of wound infection requiring additional treatment
counsel: Clean the area before applying as directed

Do not apply to the breast area if breastfeeding

pearls: Not FDA-approved; an established European/Indian topical wound-healing product (e.g., Fitostimoline) - this record reflects SmPC/manufacturer labeling
Main safety concern is allergic contact dermatitis, especially in wheat-sensitized patients
Acts locally to promote granulation and re-epithelialization; minimal systemic absorption
Available in multiple forms (cream, foam, gauze, spray) chosen by wound type
Not a substitute for appropriate antibiotic treatment of infected wounds
missed: If an application is missed, apply it as soon as remembered and continue the regular schedule. Do not apply extra to make up for a missed application.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with topical use given minimal systemic absorption. Excessive application may cause local irritation; wipe off excess and resume normal use. If accidentally ingested, provide supportive care and contact a poison control center.
